newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol off all-time highs on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Repsol off all-time highs on profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Repsol nudged lower on Friday as investors took profits after the stock hit a new all-time high on Thursday, dealers said.
"The stock has risen strongly and its normal for it to correct slightly but we're still optimistic about the firm," said a dealer at a Spanish bank.
Dealers said there were clear sell orders at prices of 6,200 pesetas, near an intraday high of 6,210.
At 1015 GMT Repsol was down 30 pesetas, 0.33 percent, to 6,120 while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up 0.27 percent to 5,503.14.
The government is selling its last 10.0 percent stake in the energy group this month, for which provisional subscriptions for the retail tranche opened on Monday.
The firm gave the first of a series of roadshows to institutional investors on Wednesday, boosting the stock to an all-time high at the close on Thursday of 6,150 pesetas.
Dealers said it was logical that the shares would pull back now, as otherwise the placement price would be too high. But the shares are still a strong investment option.
"Repsol stock is a good bet medium term. Short term we could see lower prices," a dealer at Mercavalor said.

Dealers said the retail tranche of the initial share offering is now amply covered independent of the final sale price, which might arouse concern for the placement managers that the insitutional price could be too high.
The institutional price for the fresh shares coming to the market will be set on the basis of the stock's average traded price over the period from April 21 to April 28.
